The Commodore opens the dinner with a live cheer, full of ad-libs: 'TALLY-HO! SPREAD THE BRINE, ME HEARTIES, AND MIND THE PICKLES, PRATT!' No hiccup.
The Commodore visits the galley, hefts a crock chalked '13', finds it far too heavy for marmalade, tucks it under his arm and asks who packed it. Boris says the crates came from the Captain's stores.

The Captain stands the helmsman down to sleep before the middle watch, sends him below to the crew's quarters forward, and takes the wheel himself.
The Commodore visits the bridge and tells the Captain he will scrap the Tallyho, and that they will talk about crock 13 after the show.

Leaning over the starboard rail, Boris sees two shadows on the stateroom porthole curtain: a tall one in something long to the knee, a cloak or a greatcoat, flings up an arm and swings something round at a small round one with a pointy swirl of hair on top. BONK. No face, no hat, no hands.
From the boat deck Dame Gherkina hears a hollow BONK from below and glances at her diamond wristwatch: 21:52.
Inside lifeboat 3, Percy hears a distant gong-like BONK and takes it for the ship's bell.

Counting banknotes by the rail with Dame Gherkina, Boris sees Percy creep out of lifeboat 3 for hay. All three see each other.

The heel recorder's pen swings from 8 degrees starboard to 6 degrees port. Ottilie pencils 'LURCH 22:14' on the chart.

THE GREAT LURCH. A rogue wave hits the port quarter; the Captain orders hard-a-port and brings her round, the gale comes onto the other side, and the Tallyho flips from a starboard to a port list. Every loose object aboard slides to port.
In the saloon the band, the buffet and Dame Gherkina's hat all slide to port in a single glorious crash.
In the stateroom, the sea chest skates from the starboard wall across the set marmalade until the Commodore's body stops it, and parks on his coat-tail; the smashed watch skates into the port corner.

The Captain says he must check the chart, gives Ottilie the wheel and steps through the velvet curtain; she hears the chartroom door. At 22:38, at the wheel with her back to the curtain, she hears a click, a hiss and a whirr behind it.
The bridge-wing horn bellows the cheer, hiccup and all.
The bridge-wing horn bellows the cheer, hiccup and all.
The galley horn bellows 'TALLY-HO! SPREAD THE BRINE!' with an odd hiccup in the middle. Boris shouts a gloomy 'Hurrah'.
The saloon horn bellows 'TALLY-HO! SPREAD THE BRINE!' with an odd hiccup in the middle. The saloon roars its approval: the Commodore is alive.
The Captain starts the Cheer-Box and throws the junction switch. The horns bellow the Commodore's recorded cheer.

At 22:38 the corridor horn above her bellows the Commodore's cheer, with an odd hiccup in the middle. With her ear to the door she hears nothing from inside, before, during or after it: no bellow, no stamp, and no 'HARRUMPH! WELL CHEERED, ME!', which always follows his cheer.

Word of the scream reaches the bridge. The Captain calls the helmsman up the voice-pipe, hands him the wheel and goes below.
The Captain arrives at the stateroom, orders that nobody leaves the ship (not that anybody can) and reads the watch aloud: 22:41. 'Alive at 22:38, dead by 22:41.'

The purser arrives from his office with the passenger list and the purser's book, seals the stateroom, says the wireless is dead and the police take over when we make port, and asks the detective, a guest aboard, to find out what happened.
